_comment_family: Century Gothic is Monotype's geometric sans - their answer to ITC
Avant Garde, single-storey a and all - and it ships as the old
four-style family: Regular, Bold, Italic, Bold Italic. The file in
fonts/ is the Bold, and it is named here the way montserrat-bold is
named, for the same reason and with one extra hazard on top of it.
This file's name ID 1 is 'Century Gothic', flat, with 'Bold' as its
subfamily: the Bold is one of the four styles the old family model
allows, so it answers to the family name itself. Declaring that name
would be declaring a name the Regular answers to just as well.
The extra hazard is that on this particular family that is not
hypothetical. Century Gothic has been bundled with Microsoft Office
for thirty years and is on most of the Windows machines this app runs
on - two faces in this folder already fall back to it on exactly that
reasoning (see garet-book and itc-avant-garde-std-md). So a machine
asked for 'Century Gothic' will very often answer, and what it hands
back is the Regular: a caption measured against the Bold and drawn in
a 400 would come out at a width nothing measured.
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way
montserrat-bold and telegraf-ultralight declare theirs.
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Asking for 400 here would draw this file at its own weight
under a wrong label, and asking for 800 would invite a browser to
embolden a face that is already the heavy end of its family.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under (see engine.install_fonts, which takes the
first entry); the second is the Windows full name. Both name this one
cut rather than the family, so a machine answering to either is
answering with this file - which is exactly what the fallback route is
'Century Gothic' on its own is deliberately absent, and it is the one
entry somebody will be tempted to add here because it is the name most
machines actually have the face under. It is also this file's own name
ID 1 and the name the Regular answers to, so it is the one entry that
could silently hand back a 400. The local() route is precisely where a
name that loose does its damage, since it is tried against whatever the
machine happens to have installed rather than against anything this
repo ships. It appears in the `stack` below instead, where it is a last
resort rather than a route claiming to be this file.
_comment_metrics: Four measurements, all of them for the pack that is set in this face
(content/channels/fitness-story-nw) and none of them read by anything
at run time. They are here because the next face dropped into a
Snapchat channel will want the same ones taken, which is the habit
korolev-bold started and itc-avant-garde-std-md carried on.
The cap height is 1471 units of this file's 2048-unit em, taken from
the H rather than from OS/2 because this is a version 1 OS/2 table and
sCapHeight only exists from version 2. That is 0.718 em, so at the
Snapchat preset's stated 40px the capitals stand 28.7px tall - between
Garamond Premier's 660-per-1000 and ITC Avant Garde's 740, and near
enough to the latter that a caption here reads about as large as one on
FeedDrama. The x-height is 1088, which is 0.531 em and is the enlarged
x-height this design was modified for; it is never drawn under the
preset's `uppercase` and is noted only because it is what makes the
face look set large in the text box while the canvas sets capitals.
The widths are a plain sum of advance widths, and on this file that is
exactly what the browser will measure: there is no kern table and no
GPOS in it at all, so there is no pairing for a canvas to apply and
nothing for the sum to be missing. Worth one line because it is not
true of most of this folder - itc-avant-garde-std-md had to measure on
a canvas to find out that its GPOS changed nothing.
This face is WIDE, which is the number to know before setting a
caption in it. Twenty mixed capitals (A to T) measure 501.6px against
the 486px a Snapchat line has, so like ITC Avant Garde it puts the
frame's width and the preset's twenty-character ceiling in the same
place instead of the characters binding first. Real sentences of twenty
characters come out between 427px and 496px depending on what letters
are in them - the spaces and the narrow letters an alphabet run has
none of do most of the work - so an unusually round line breaks at
nineteen instead of twenty, which the wrapper does on its own and
nobody sees (see the two ceilings in js/caption.js).
The glyph check the Snapchat packs take: 668 codepoints, the accented
Latin capitals and lower case among them, plus the curly apostrophe the
rewrite elides with. A caption with a name in it is therefore drawn
from this file rather than from whatever the browser substitutes for a
missing glyph, which would be a different face at a width nothing
measured.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and this is the one
face in the folder whose nearest fallback is its own family.
'Century Gothic' second, which is the name kept out of `local` above
and belongs here for the same reason it was kept out of there. In
`local` it is a claim that the machine has THIS file; here it is an
admission that the file is gone and that the machine may have the
Regular, which the browser will embolden at the 700 asked for. That is
a synthesised weight at a width nothing measured, which is broken - but
it is the same skeleton, the same circles and the same single-storey a,
and it is the closest thing a Windows machine with Office on it can be
asked for.
Segoe UI stands behind it for the machine that somehow lacks even that,
and Arial behind that; both have a real Bold, so the weight survives as
far as the substitute family has the weight to survive it. Impact and
Arial Black are absent for telegraf-ultralight's reason - they are
heavy condensed display cuts, and putting one behind a geometric built
on circles would make the one thing that survives a missing file the
furthest possible thing from it.
stack: 'Century Gothic Bold', 'Century Gothic', 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif
